title: Seller cheatsheet: data flow, telemetry & audit-log claims
content:
Purpose:
This one-page (long) seller-facing brief equips AEs, CSEs and solutions engineers with concise, defensible language about Redwood's data handling, audit logging, and compliance posture for SOC2/ISO/HIPAA conversations. It focuses on the buyer questions we see in late-stage POC/RFPs and provides recommended claim language + evidence pointers and competitive differentiators.

Audience:
- Sales and CSEs responding to infosec and compliance teams
- Pre-sales engineers prepping for technical evals

High-level positioning (1-2 lines):
- Redwood provides production-grade inference with auditable telemetry and exportable audit logs, backed by SOC2 controls, optional ISO27001 alignment, and a HIPAA-ready operating profile for private deployments. We separate control plane telemetry (Redwood-managed) from customer data plane (which can remain inside customer VPCs for Private deployments).

Top buyer FAQs and short, safe answers (one-liners you can say live):
- How do you handle customer prompts and outputs?
  "Prompts and generated outputs are ephemeral by default in hosted mode; customers can opt-in to retention for diagnostics. For Private deployments, customer data never leaves their VPC unless explicitly routed."
- Do you retain PII or PHI by default?
  "No. By default, we do not retain customer content beyond transient caching for inference; retention is configurable and we provide deletion controls and exportable retention policies."
- Can we get raw audit logs for model usage?
  "Yes. We provide structured, exportable audit logs containing request metadata, model variant, latency, and anonymized token counts; in Dedicated/Private modes those logs can be routed to the customer's SIEM or object store."
- Are audit logs tamper-evident?
  "Logs are write-once within our logging pipeline and we offer cryptographic checksums for long-term retention on request as part of our enterprise package."

Claims with evidence mapping (what to say + where to point):
- Claim: SOC2 Type II controls over availability and confidentiality.
  Evidence: SOC2 report (redacted), control matrix, SOC2 scope doc (Confluence: RGW-SEC-AUDIT-2025).
- Claim: ISO27001 alignment available for enterprise customers.
  Evidence: ISO readiness summary, external audit plan (internal roadmap link).
- Claim: HIPAA-ready private deployment (customer-managed network + HSM/KMS integration).
  Evidence: HIPAA architecture diagram, BAAs, KMS/HSM integration guide, customer deployment checklist.
- Claim: Exportable, structured audit logs with request-level metadata.
  Evidence: sample log schema (attached JSON), S3 delivery playbook, SIEM ingestion docs.

How to handle the tricky questions (scripted responses):
- Q: "Can you guarantee zero-model-training-on-customer-data?"
  Script: "We treat customer content as belonging to customers. For hosted API, we have an explicit policy and contractual promise not to use customer prompts/outputs to train our public models. For enterprise customers requiring assurance, we support Private deployments and dedicated capacity where data never leaves customer-controlled networks."
- Q: "What about insider access to customer content?"
  Script: "Access is governed by role-based controls, MFA, and just-in-time approval flows. All access to production logs and artifacts is logged and regularly reviewed as part of our SOC2 control program."

Competitive differentiators to highlight (short bullets):
- Unlike pure public-API players, Redwood can run in customer VPCs with the same API surface — lowers legal friction and simplifies BAAs.
- Compared to self-hosted open-source runtimes, Redwood provides SLA-backed latency and automated kernel/quantization tuning that reduces operator burden.
- Our audit-log export and SIEM integration is designed for token-level cost attribution and troubleshooting, not just authentication events — helps buyers reconcile spend and performance quickly.

Typical red flags and how to mitigate them (prep lines):
- Buyer asks for "full access to internal monitoring dashboards": offer scoped exports and dashboards, propose an on-site demo or read-only role with recorded sessions.
- Buyer requires immutable, long-term archival: propose S3+Glacier export with checksum and retention policy; offer evidence of retention tests.
- Buyer demands custom logging fields: accept small mapping work under implementation plan; highlight standard schema covers the 90% needs (request id, model id, timestamp, latency, token counts, redaction flags).

Sample audit-log plain-English claim set (short bullets for slides):
- "Every inference request logs request-id, model-variant, timestamp, latency, region, and token metrics; logs are exportable to your cloud."
- "Audit logs can be routed to customer S3 buckets or SIEMs in Dedicated/Private modes; hosted customers can request scheduled exports."
- "We provide redaction and PII flags during log ingestion to avoid storing sensitive tokens in plain text."

Evidence checklist to attach to RFP responses (quick QA):
- Available: SOC2 Type II report (redacted) — point to Confluence and legal.
- Available: Architecture diagrams for Private deployment and BAA template.
- Available: Sample audit log schema + 7-day sample (anonymized).
- Available on request: Cryptographic checksum procedure for long-term archive.
- To be scheduled: ISO certification timeline (if buyer requires certificate now, present mitigation plan).

Negotiation and SLA playbook (practical tips):
- Start with standard contract language: data exclusivity, retention defaults, export rights.
- For high-risk buyers, propose Dedicated with VPC peering and pre-commit capacity — easier compliance fit than hosted.
- Use evidence-first approach: share redacted SOC2 immediately, propose technical onboarding call to walk through logs/export mechanics.

Appendix: quick rebuttals and shortcuts for reps
- If buyer is concerned about model drift from customer data: "We do not use customer prompts for public model training; model updates are controlled and documented in release notes."
- If buyer wants API-level encryption in flight and at rest: "TLS for in-flight and AES-256 (or customer KMS) for at-rest by default; details in KMS integration guide."

Closing: one-paragraph framing for executive slides
Redwood is a production-first inference platform that separates deployment modes to match buyer risk profiles: hosted for fast proofs with clear retention controls, Dedicated for SLA-backed, auditable capacity, and Private for customers with strict network or regulatory requirements. Our audit logging is focused on operational and compliance usefulness — exportable, structured, and designed to integrate with existing SIEM and archival workflows. Point customers to the SOC2 report, the Private deployment architecture, and the audit-log schema during diligence to accelerate security approvals.
